translation:
Everything rests upon this principle.

_Om pranav pura hot hai, ra ra ma maa dou sees. Tulsi ek rakar bin, omkar anish._ (Tulsidas says: the Pranav Om becomes complete with the two syllables ra-ra and ma-ma; without the single syllable ra, says Tulsi, the Omkar is without its Lord.)

Tulsidas says that the three-gunas-natured Omkar, embodying the three deities, reaches its limit at the boundary formed by the "ra" of Rarankar and the "ma" of Makar. Thus, without the presence of Rarankar, the Ekankar alone -- without the Rarankar of the Supreme Being -- is powerless, meaningless, and useless.

_Au(ya)ukar akar makar, e teeno maya joi. Maya hoi kari vistarya, gyani aape soi._ (Gyaniji Maharaj says: know that these three -- the "u," the "a," and the "m" of Om -- are Maya; having become Maya, they have spread themselves through the three gunas, and this the knower himself has seen.)

Gyaniji Maharaj says that the "u," the "a," and the "m" that make up this Om should be known as the threefold Maya of the three gunas; this Omkar spreads through the world in the form of Maya, by way of the three gunas of sattva, rajas, and tamas -- and this Gyaniji himself has witnessed directly.

_Kabir gorakhku gam nahi, shankar pahuche nahi, taha kabira ram rahya, rarankarme mahi._ (Servant Kabir says: even Gorakh cannot fathom it, even Shankar cannot reach it -- there, in the very midst of Rarankar, Kabir revels.)

Servant Kabirji says that the Rarankari principle of the Lord cannot be grasped even by the followers of the Gorakh sect, and it is within this Rarankar that Kabirji is reveling in bliss.

_Kishandev govardhan dharyo, dronagiri hanuman, sheshnag sir medini, ab dhariye kiska dhyan._ (Krishna held up Govardhan mountain, Hanuman held up the Dronagiri mountain, Sheshnag holds the earth upon his head -- now whose meditation should one hold?)

Santdas says that Shri Krishna held up Govardhan mountain, and Hanuman held up the Dronachal mountain; Sheshnag has held the earth upon his head -- so, among these, whom should we regard as the greatest, to whose meditation, remembrance, and worship should we devote ourselves?

_Hanuman hari bhagat hai, kishandev avtar, sheshnag sumran kare, rarankar kartar._ (Hanuman is a devotee of Hari, Krishna is the very incarnation of God; Sheshnag does remembrance of Rarankar, the Creator.)

Santdas says that Hanuman is a devotee of Ram, while Krishna is himself an incarnation of God. Sheshnag, by remembering God who abides in the form of Rarankar, is able to hold up the earth.

_Joti sarupi ram hai, ekohi rarankar, aur sabhi santdas, mayaka ravistar._ (Ram is of the nature of light -- He alone is the Rarankar; all else, says Santdas, is the spreading of Maya.)

Santdas says that Lord Ram is the divine principle of the nature of light; that Ram and Rarankar are one and the same divine principle. Everything else -- including the Omkar and so forth -- is only the spreading-out of Maya.

_Prem joti parmeshwar, taasko naam rarankar, shunyamani._ (The light of love is the Supreme Lord; the name of that light is Rarankar, the sound arising in the Void.)

Servant Kabirji says in this rekhta (a lyrical verse-form) that the radiance of the light of loving devotion to God is itself the form of the Supreme Lord, and the name of that light of love is Rarankar -- its sound is the symbol, in the form of Shabda-Brahma (the Word-Brahman), of the formless Supreme Brahman.

In the Bhagwati Katha, part 32, page 204, Prabhudutt writes: "There is a saying: 'Wrestlers have many wrestlers greater than them -- if not in their own house, then plenty can be found outside it.' That is to say, in this world there are many warriors greater than the warriors who fight, only they may not be found in one's own house or town -- but on searching, many will be found in the world. The Ganga thought, 'I am the greatest,' but Shivji held her within his matted locks, so Shivji became the greater one. Shivji, too, is upheld by Kailash, so Kailash became the greater one. Kailash was lifted up in play by Ravana, so Ravana became the greater one. Ravana was pinned under Bali's armpit, so Bali became the greater one. And Bali was slain by the Lord with a single arrow. Thus we see that in this world, none but God Himself can claim to be the very greatest of all."

In notebook (litiyu) no. 49, pages 33-34, Revered Yadunath has written down the following sakhis of Santdas concerning Rarankar.

_Swarag madhe patalme, dhru shiv shesh nihar, teen lok hai santdas, e rarankar aadhar. ||1||_ (In heaven, in the midst, and in the netherworld -- Dhruv, Shiv, and Shesh behold it; the three worlds, says Santdas, rest upon this Rarankar as their support.)

Santdas says: in the middle of the heavens [unclear] -- the mortal, earthly world, or the netherworld -- Dhruvji is in the sky; in the midst of the heavens, Shivji is on Kailash; and Sheshnag is in the netherworld. These deities who are dwelling and keeping watch -- all three worlds continue to endure resting upon the support of that Rarankar, the form of the one Brahman, namely Ram.

_Rarankarku kahat hai, brahm sarupi ram, santdas tihu lokme, sabhi iska kaam. ||2||_ (Rarankar, it is said, has the form of Brahma as Ram; says Santdas, in all three worlds, everything is His doing.)

Santdas says that Rarankar is said to have the form of Parabrahma Paramatma Ram. The creation of all the three worlds -- heaven, the mortal world, and the netherworld -- is the work that Ram has done.

_Ram angji rakhiya, kooti rahya shir kaal, sab santanka santdas, rarankar richhpal. ||3||_ (Ram has kept His devotees safe; Time stands pounding at their head in vain; Rarankar, says Santdas, is the protector of all the saints.)

Ram Himself is Angaji -- that is, He is the one who cannot be conquered -- and He alone is the protector of the saints. The abode of Rarankar lies deep within. Do not lose faith in it.

Note -- Revered Yadunath Maharaj used to say that the followers of the Radhaswami tradition count Rarankar as occupying the fourth stage among their seven planes (bhumika), and on that basis they regard Jivanji as incomplete. But in explaining this to the devotees, Revered Yadunath says: do not, under the delusion that "Jivanji is incomplete," lose your faith in Rarankar. Rarankar is nothing less than the complete, perfect form of God Himself.

By taking the Name of God, joy does not come to so many households.

_Liya naam nirvan uta ghar anand na hoi, kampe tanka karn bharmana bhagat roi, moh rahyo shirkoot nikat maya nahi aave, aandev kar jodi dekhi vandan kari aave, ram charan rane bhajya jam dar upaje shog, kaha janu e ramjan kita udhar log._ (Charandasji says: in taking the final, supreme, most excellent Name of God, joy and gladness do not arise in the households of so many kinds of people. Yet for the fortunate ones who do take this Name, the karmas of the body and doubts flee away weeping in sorrow, and delusion, helpless, beats its own head and runs away -- the maya of delusion cannot come near one who takes that Name. Those defeated come bowing in surrender to God. Whoever has done bhajan of Ram -- Yamaraja himself, fearing him, feels grief at approaching him. Thus, who can know how many such devotees of Ram have brought about the deliverance of countless others?)

Charandasji says that in taking this final, supreme, most excellent Name of God, joy and gladness do not arise in the households of so many kinds of people. For those who do take this Name, the karmas of their body and their doubts flee away weeping in sorrow, and delusion, helpless, beats its own head and flees away. Delusion and maya cannot come near one who takes that Name. Such beings, defeated, come bowing in surrender to God. Whoever has practiced the remembrance of Ram, from him even Yamaraja shrinks back in fear and grieves. Thus, who can know how many people the devotees of Ram must have delivered?

Revered Yadunath wrote the above passage in notebook 49, pages 33-34. In connection with it, he has given a further explanation on page 32. "I had gone to give a katha (religious discourse) at Patra. Revered Yadunath, who had suffered a paralytic stroke, used to sit together with me." In connection with that katha of his, he wrote the following on page 32.

Samvat 2020, Posh Sud 12, Friday, Ramdhun day 2.

"Jai to Jivanji Maharaj. Yesterday, in the course of Shri Jagdishchandra's discourse, on the occasion arising, I drew attention to the word 'Rarankar'; the listeners among the audience who reflect deeply will surely remember it."

Having written thus, he wrote down and presented the sayings of Santdas and Charandasji on Rarankar; his endorsement of their words is as follows.

It is a matter of wonder that Revered Shri Yadunath must have kept in memory all these sayings made by these saints, for he had written the sayings of Santdas and Charandas in his notebook and recited them aloud to the devotees. Blessed indeed is Revered Yadunath Maharaj.

_Tu tu tu tu hot hai, hu nahi ek vaar, sadguru antare jivana, so japat hai rarankar._ (It becomes only "You, You, You, You" -- "I" is not there even once. He within whom the Sadguru's teaching abides, says Jivan, is the one who chants Rarankar.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: by continually remembering You, I became absorbed into You, and within me, quite naturally, no trace of "I"-ness, ego, or possessiveness remained. Whoever carries the Sadguru's command within their heart continues to chant and repeat Rarankar.

_Oaukarme aathde, sur brahma munidev, rarankarme jivana, je lagya sadguru sev._ (The gods, Brahma, and the sage-deities wander lost within the Omkar; those who have devoted themselves to the Sadguru's service, says Jivan, dwell within Rarankar.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says that the gods, Brahma, and the great sages keep wandering lost in the triguna-natured Maya of the Omkar; but those who have devoted themselves to bhakti of the Sadguru remain engaged in the remembrance of Rarankar.

_Oaukarthi upanyo, jivan jug sansar, rarankarthi upanyo, sadguru parivar._ (From the Omkar, says Jivan, the world of the ages arose; from Rarankar arose the family of the Sadguru.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says that this entire world has manifested from the Omkar; but the family of the Sadguru has manifested from Rarankar, the principle that is beyond the three gunas.

_Ek aksharthe jivana bhayo brahmand vistar, raro rakhyo harijan, mamo bhayo sansar._ (From the one syllable, says Jivan, the whole expanse of the universe came to be; the "ra" was kept by the Harijans, while the "ma" became the world.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says that from the single Omkar of the imperishable divine principle, this universe has spread out; but the Harijans (devotees) have embraced the Rarankari principle of God, while it is from the Maya of the Omkar that this world has been fashioned.

_Pothi parbrahm naamki, sadguru dai batay, aad avinashi jivana, rare mame jitt laay._ (The scripture of the Parabrahma's Name has been given and shown by the Sadguru; O soul, fix your mind, from the very beginning, in the imperishable -- in the "ra" and the "ma.")

Jivandasji Maharaj says: the Sadguru has shown us the instructive scripture that is the Name of Parabrahma Paramatma; fix your mind solely on the chanting of that Name of Ram, in whom, as the primal Supreme Being, both the "ra" and the "ma" are present.

_Bavan akshar jivana, ek akshar tattvasar, mama pahelo je lakhyo, teh no ved na paave paar._ (Of the fifty-two letters, says Jivan, only one letter is the very essence of the truth; the one written just before the "ma" -- even the Vedas cannot fathom its depth.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says that among the fifty-two root letters of the alphabet, only a single letter is the truly excellent one -- and that is the "r" of Rarankar which stands before the "m" of the name Ram, prior to the Omkar; even the Vedas cannot know the mystery of it.

_Lau lagi hari naamki, rom rom rarankar, sahaje sumran hot hai, bisrat nahi lagar._ (When the deep absorption of Hari's Name has taken hold, Rarankar dwells in every pore of the body; remembrance then arises effortlessly, and is never forgotten, not even for a moment.)

Gyaniji Maharaj says that when one becomes wholly absorbed through devotion to the resounding of God's Name, the chanting of Rarankar continues in every single pore of the body. In such an effortless, natural state, the remembrance of Hari happens of its own accord, and one never forgets the Name of God even for an instant.

_Shesh sahastra mukh do jivha, jape so rarankar, shiv shakti amar bhaye, sau jivana pran aadhar._ (Sheshnag, with two tongues in each of his thousand mouths, chants that Rarankar; through it, says Jivan, Shiva and Shakti became immortal, for it is the support of the very life-breath.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says that Sheshnag, with the two tongues present in each of the mouths of his thousand hoods, continually chants this divine Name. By the glory of that Rarankar, even Shiva and Parvati have become great and immortal. That divine Name, Rarankar, is exceedingly dear to Jivanji Maharaj.

_Ooch bhaya to ka bhaya, rom rom rarankar, tulsi harikee bhagati bin, chare jaat chamar._ (What good is it to be born high, unless Rarankar dwells in every pore? Says Tulsi: without devotion to Hari, all four castes are but cobblers.)

Tulsidas says: even if a person belongs to a high-born family, be it a Brahmin, a Vaishya, or the like, what real gain has been achieved thereby? It carries no meaning at all. Everyone must make the devotion to Rarankar pervade every pore of their body; otherwise, without this Rarankari devotion to God, people of all four varnas are just as base as a cobbler.

The saints have made a division (bhaanjani, that is, a splitting or apportioning into greater and lesser shares) between Rarankar and Makar: Makar is of the nature of Maya, while Rarankar is the full and complete Brahman -- this is what the saints have grasped and accepted. (From Kuvarpura's Bhagwan Shyamji's Samagam, book no. 2, page 414.)

_Raakaro uchchaar maatram bahirjaat kampatek, punah pravesh na kartabhye, makaro cha kapaatvat._ (By the mere utterance of the syllable "ra," sins go out and depart; and so that they may not enter back in again, the syllable "ma" becomes, as it were, a lid closing them out.)

_Kabir rarankar uchcharte, nikasat paap aghor, mudan dwar makarsu, nahi pesanku thaur._ (Servant Kabir says: on uttering Rarankar, the most terrible sins go out; the door is then sealed shut by the Makar, and there remains no place for them to re-enter.)

Servant Kabirji says that by uttering Rarankar, terrible sins go out from within; and then, since the door is shut with the Makar, they can no longer find any way to re-enter from anywhere.

_Sandh garad akhar raro, jag adh deve bhagaae, dhandas vai dwaarku, mamoki paar lagaaye._ (The letter "r," like a lion's roar, drives away even sins as mighty as an elephant. Therefore, Dhandas says, the door of the mouth should then be closed shut by uttering the "m.")

_Tulsi rakar uchcharte, paap gaye ek vaar, funi pravesh na karashke, jad makarki vaat._ (Tulsi says: by uttering "ra," sin departs at once; so that it may never enter again, fix the bolt of Makar upon the path.)

Tulsidas says that by uttering the "r," sin departs once and for all; and so that it may not enter back in again, fix the bolt of the Makar upon the pathway of the mouth.

_Kabir rakarke uchcharte, adh bikal chale bhagajyu mahe, mant makar pat mundade, to nij bhasim hoy jaay._

Servant Kabirji says that by uttering the "r," whatever sin dwells within us grows agitated and flees away; and if, through the technique of the mantra, it is then sealed shut by the covering of the Makar, that sin is itself reduced to ash and destroyed.

Handwritten notebook 33, page 179, Sakhi 2.

_Kabir shivam viranchi sanakadik, surnar muni apaar, kahai kabir surta sabai, bakta ohankaar._ (Servant Kabir says: Shiva, Brahma, Sanak and the other sages, and countless gods, men, and munis -- all, though absorbed, merely prattle empty talk of "I-am".)

Servant Kabirji says that Shiva, Brahma, Sanak and the other sages, gods, human beings, and countless multitudes of munis -- all of them, though absorbed, keep uttering useless, empty prattle of the Omkar.

_Onkar vriksh trailokya shakha jugchaar patram rachite vidhaata, swaadrishta anekam phalaeksh ekam, bhujo ram krishnam bhedaanabheda._ (Omkar is the tree, the three worlds are its branches, the four ages are its leaves. Thus it appears in many forms, yet its aim is but one. Worship that Ram-Krishna who is one single form, in whom no distinction of any kind exists.)

_Omkar phal deetate, upaje ichchha jhaad, sadguru kahe sadbhaavso, nishche nejo gaad. ||17||_ (From the stalk of the Omkar's fruit, the tree of desire springs up; the Sadguru says, with true sincerity, plant firmly the banner of resolve.)

Servant Kabirji says that from the stalk-bearing fruit of Omkar, the tree of desire is produced. Therefore the Sadguru, moved with feeling, says: plant firmly, like a spear, the banner of steadfast resolve; resolve within your heart to practice loving devotion. Do not become entangled in the Omkar, for it produces the tree that is the web of the world's Maya, made of Omkar-born desires.

_Chetanah shashvatah shanto vyomaateeto nirunjanah, bindunaadakalaateetastasmai shri gurave namah. ||153||_ (Salutations to that revered Guru who is of the nature of pure consciousness, eternal, greater even than the sky, and untainted [the Maya-free Brahman], who is beyond the arts of the Pranav's light.)

In Raag Ramgri.

_Dhyan dhar dhyan dhar Ramjina naamnu, Ramjina naame sansar chhoote. Naam visaar tum saadhan shu karo, naamna dhyan bina kaam na khoote. ||Tek||_
_Naamnu dhyan Shesh Shankar Dhruv Prahlad kidhu, naamna dhyane moh janjeer chhoote. ||1||_
_Naam bisaari roopne dhyaane te vilagya, tehne tattva te naare ladhe. ||2||_
_Saroopnu dhyan to aave ne jaaye, naamnu dhyan rarankar gaave. ||3||_
_Bhan Narsaiyo mune tattva ladhyu, naamnu sharan maru man bandhyu. ||4||_

(O soul, meditate, meditate on the Name of Ramji; through the Name of Ramji this worldly ocean is crossed. If you forsake the Name, what other true means will you find? Without meditation on the Name, endeavor never ceases. Refrain.
1. Meditation on the Name was practiced by Sheshnag, Shankar, Dhruv, and Prahlad; through meditation on the Name, the chain of delusion is broken.
2. Those who, forgetting the Name, become attached to meditating on form alone -- they never attain the truth.
3. Meditation on a manifest form comes and goes, but meditation on the Name sings of Rarankar itself.
4. Narsaiyo declares: I have attained the truth; I have bound my mind in the refuge of the Name.)

O soul! Meditate upon the Name of God, the Name of Ram; practice devotion to Ram. Through the Name of Ram, the ocean of this world will be crossed. Leaving aside the Name of Ram, is there any better worship you could perform? Without meditation on the Name of Ram, if one undertakes all manner of other spiritual practices, then the doing of countless different rites will never cease, and thereby one's deliverance will not come about. Meditation and devotion, remembrance of the Name of Ram -- this was undertaken by Sheshnag, Shankar, Dhruv, Prahlad, and others. Through devotion to Ram, the chain of the world's delusion and Maya will be released. If, forgetting the Name of Ram, one clings to the worship of a perishable form endowed with qualities, one will not attain the eternal, supreme divine principle. The divine form endowed with qualities and shape takes incarnation and comes, and then departs again; but devotion to the divine Name, the Name of Ram, reveals the eternal divine principle beyond the three gunas, namely Rarankar. Narsinh Mehta says: I have attained this eternal, Rarankar-natured divine principle; therefore I have fixed my mind wholly in the refuge of God's Name.

In Raag Maru.

_Sidh na hoy re Shreepatne, sidh na hoy re, vaishnav vina taryo na koy re. ||Tek||_
_Kahoji kiyo re sannyasi sharan ja paamyo, dand vesh jataa dhaari re, tamo vaishnavoni ninda karo chho, bhundo narakno adhikaari re. ||1||_
_Tamaari stree mare tyaare khaava tale, tavaaraa bhaguvaan pehero re, preet bhagat vairaag vina, phunkyo kaano ja bahero re. ||Shri||2||_
_Tamaaraa oaunkaranu karo ke athaanu, maahaare vrindaavan chalo re, bhane Narsaiyo mahelo dand kamandal, maahaari puthe taal vajaado re. ||3||_

(Through this Shripat, the human birth cannot be made fruitful, nor can true liberation ever be attained -- for without Vaishnavism, none has ever crossed the ocean of worldly existence. Refrain.
1. Tell me yourself: which sannyasi has ever attained the refuge of Lord Vishnu? You sannyasis bear the staff and the matted locks, and you revile the Vaishnavas -- you are wicked ones, deserving to suffer hell.
2. When your wife dies, and restlessness comes over you, then you put on the ochre robes; but without true loving devotion and without renunciation, you have merely had a mantra whispered into a deaf man's ear.
3. Whatever pickle you make of your Omkar, as for me, come to Vrindavan with me. Narsaiyo declares: set down your staff and water-pot, and follow behind me, playing the cymbals.)

Narsinh Mehta was, on the instructions of seventeen sannyasis, harassed by King Mandalik for a garland. At that time Narsinh Mehta sang the songs of the Haarmaala (Garland). Among these, this song was sung addressed to a sannyasi named Shripat. In it he says: alas, through this "Shripat," the human birth will not be made fruitful, and true good end cannot ever be attained, because none has ever escaped the ocean of worldly existence without Vaishnavism. He asks: tell me yourself, which sannyasi (a follower of the Shiva path) has ever attained the refuge of Lord Vishnu? You sannyasis bear the staff or matted locks and revile the Vaishnavas -- such wicked people as you deserve to suffer a base hell. When your wife has died, and you feel restless, you then don ochre robes; but if true love for devotion has not awakened in you, and your attachments have not been removed, then you are as ignorant as one whom the guru who gave you the vows of renunciation has made into a disciple merely by whispering a secret mantra into a deaf man's ear. Thus, this Omkar to which you cling -- just as it stores up useless things, you too uselessly and vainly cling to this useless Omkar. If you truly desire devotion, then come with me to the land of Vrindavan, marked by loving devotion; set down this staff and water-pot of yours, and follow my example, becoming absorbed in loving devotion, and take up the cymbals and the pakhawaj drum for bhajan-kirtan (devotional singing).

Thus, in explaining the importance of Rarankar, which points to the Name of Ram, it was said in the Samagam that the Name of Ram alone truly serves to carry one across the ocean of worldly existence, while the Omkar cannot carry one across that ocean. And an illustration of a great soul (Mahapurush) was given: a great soul had once written the Name of Ram on the palm of a hunter's hand, so that he was able to walk upon the waters of a river; but midway across, curiosity arose in him as to just what the great soul had written that enabled him to walk upon the water. So he looked at his hand, and saw that the Name of Ram was written there; and it occurred to his mind, "Why, this is something I already know!" Thus a disregard for the Name of Ram arose in him, and he began to sink. In this way, because worldly people, by regarding the Name of Ram as something ordinary, give greater importance to the Omkar, efforts have been made -- for the very purpose of increasing the perceived importance of the Omkar -- to adorn the Omkar outwardly, so as to conceal the truth and make it appear precious and highly important. Therefore it was said in the Samagam that just as ordinary, coarse cloth, if made to look golden in appearance, comes to be valued more highly, so too has an effort been made to embellish the Omkar in this same way.

It has been said in the Samagam that in this connection Jivandasji stated that when Janakji emptied out twenty-eight tanks (kunda), that too was by the glory of the Name of Ram, and so on; and again, just as the hunter, taking the Name of Ram written by the great soul, walked upon the water and then said, "Why, this I already know" -- he did not reach the far shore, and was swept away. Moreover, whoever holds such an attitude in mind belongs to the ordinary worldly-minded. For such people, the Omkar was elevated, and the Name was made heavy; an effort was made to establish the Omkar as more precious, in the way that coarse cloth, when it is set in a mounting of gold, fetches a higher price, while set in a cheap mounting it fetches only a low price -- and again, when a gemstone is set in a heavy, ornate mounting, its price rises. In just this way, efforts have been made to embellish the mantra of the Omkar outwardly and thereby raise its perceived worth.

It is said in verse 15 of the Ishavasya Upanishad:

_Hiranyamayena patrena satyasyaapihitam mukham, tatvam pushanapaavrinu satyadharmaaya drashtaye. ||15||_ (The true substance that is the Self lies covered by the golden, glittering lid of worldly Maya. O Pusha [the presiding deity of worldly wealth, the Sun] -- remove that covering, so that the vision of the true principle may be revealed to us.)

Thus, a false rumor has been spread that the Omkar, adorned with an illusory brilliance made to resemble Brahman itself, is of the highest order; the Name of God has been mixed together with the Omkar, and thereby the Omkar has been made to appear weighty.

_Man mevaasi vakadiya, bharami naamme bhaar, bhaanj ghad paancho kari, tab sadguru kiya karaar. ||78||_

Servant Kabirji says: the mind, deceitful like a crane appearing pure and white, attached a burden of delusion to the greatness of the divine Name; when the five kinds of sense-objects created the disturbance of doubt and conflicting resolve within it, then the Sadguru made a pledge to redeem us through the divine Name.

_Vaki niksi bahutsi, paauke ko nahi thaam, thode dhani nibediya, guru bhaye na sa jamaan. ||79||_

Servant Kabirji says that through these five sense-objects, a great deal of turmoil and delusion arose, so that no firm and settled footing could be attained; even a slight but strong bondage to the sense-objects separated him from devotion to God, and so the Guru did not stand as surety to rescue him from that bondage.

This is a portion of a tale found in the glorification (mahatmya) of Kartak Vad 11; it is called Utpatti Ekadashi ("the Ekadashi of Origin"). (Register no. 874, pages 216-217.) That Omkar mantra, given by Brahma -- having received it, Brahma first performed austerities. There, its glory arose in his mind, so that he came to feel he was like God himself. All around was water. At that time Kripanath (the Merciful Lord) arrived there, and shook his right ear, from which a bubble of water arose. Brahma was watching; just then it burst, and from within it a child appeared. In the twinkling of an eye, it grew into a full-grown being. Bearing weapons, it spoke, and Brahma said, "Take up your weapon." Brahmaji was struck with wonder. Brahmaji fled; looking behind, he saw no one; ahead, he saw Mahadevji. The two of them met and fought a great battle. Then, both of them, growing weary, fled from him. Even so, this demon, named Madhukaitabh, pursued them and continued to wage great war. At that time, Govindji, mounted on Garuda, arrived, and told Rudra and Brahma to turn back; but having fought, they instead fled and entered a cave in the Mahendrachal mountain. Madhukaitabh released great arrows. At that time Rudra and Brahma, in order to defeat the demon, offered praise to Kripanath. In place of his wrath, a maiden appeared before Kripanath, and she said, "Maharaj, what is your command?" Then Kripanath said, "Slay the demon Madhukaitabh." She then waged a great battle, and that maiden slew Madhukaitabh. The name of that maiden was Ekadashi. Then the demon's flesh floated upon the water, and from it came what is known as the earth of fifty crore yojanas in extent. Then the guardians of the ten directions (Dikpalas) were placed, who are in the form of elephants, and who hold up the earth with their trunks -- for they hold it up with their trunks so that it may not shake or shift. Then, when a dip occurred in the middle of the earth, Mount Meru was set there. Then Rudra was given Kailash.

When Brahma arose from the navel-lotus of the Lord Narayana, dirt fell from the Lord's nose, and from it two demons named Madhu and Kaitabh were born; they began to fight with Brahma. Brahma, defeated by them and distressed, began to praise Vishnu. Vishnu, awakening from His yoga-sleep (mohanidra), manifested a maiden named Krutya, and through her slew Madhukaitabh. Because Vishnu destroyed the demon named Madhu, He is called Madhusudan. In the Brahmavaivarta Purana it is said that by slaying the demon named Madhu -- that is, by destroying the "madhu" (wine/intoxicant) in the form of good and evil -- this Madhu, which used to destroy the dharma of devotees, and which is an action that, though it appears as sweet as honey at first, has an evil result for worldly people in the end -- by destroying this, Lord Vishnu is called Madhusudan.

The earth, formed from the flesh of Madhu, was made steady by the Dikpalas and Mount Meru, and Kailash was then given to Rudra -- of this same matter is the following Rameni (a verse-form) of Servant Kabirji.

Rameni.

_Gaye jug saath jaat ham jaanya, sat sukritka udhra paana. ||1||_
_Dekh paana tab kin vichaara, upji srishti rachyo sansaara. ||2||_
_Chohodas paniya agam gambheera, bohot jatan kari raakho neera. ||3||_
_Page hukam dhartiku kino, taari sumer pomi par dino. ||4||_
_Na hote brahma na hote mahesha, aadya anta na hote ganesha. ||5||_
_Sat sukrite ek agya kini, brahmapuri brahme lakshya dini. ||6||_
_Narad brahmae kiya vichaara, kaalke haath diya sansaara. ||7||_

Sakhi: _Re re kaal apradhiya, durlabh tor na sharir, sat sukritki naavari, so khele daas kabir._

(1. When sixty ages had passed away, we came to know that the good fortune of true righteous action had now opened up.
2. Seeing this opportunity for righteous action, He resolved to arise, and by that resolve, this creation was fashioned: "I am alone; let me become many."
3. The waters of the great dissolution were, on every side, unfathomably deep; with great effort, that water was held back and restrained.
4. First of all, the command was given to the earth -- the earth was rescued from the water, and Mount Meru was set upon it and made steady.
5. At that time, neither Brahma nor Mahesh had yet come into being; from the very beginning to the end, not even a Ganapati existed.
6. The true, righteous Parabrahma, of the nature of true reality, gave a single command, and with that will, took up the intention of setting the creation of the universe into motion.
7. Narada and Brahmaji reflected that this Lord had made this world subject to Time.
Sakhi: O Time, you sinner! Do not destroy this rare, hard-to-obtain body; for Servant Kabir plays upon the boat of true righteous action.)

Servant Kabirji says that when sixty ages had passed, it became known to them that the destiny of true righteous action had now opened up; seeing this occasion for righteous action, He made the decision to arise, and because of this, He fashioned this creation, thinking: "I am alone, so let Me become many." The waters of the dissolution were, on every side, so deep that no bounds could be found; that water was held back only through great effort. And first of all, a command was given to the earth -- the earth was rescued from the water and made steady, with Mount Meru set upon it. At that time, neither had Brahma come into being, nor had Shiva come into being; from beginning to end there was not even anything like a Ganapati. The true, righteous Parabrahma, of genuine and true nature, having given a single command and formed the will, took up into contemplation the setting-in-motion of the creation of the universe. Narada and Brahmaji reflected that this God had made this world subject to Time.

_Adyaiva hasitam geetam pathitam yah shariribhih, adyaiva te na drashyante kashtam kaalasya cheshtitam._ (Those who were, this very day, laughing with this same body, singing beautiful songs, reciting the finest verses -- who knows where they have this very day vanished? Now their body, made of the five elements, is nowhere to be seen at all. Alas! How harsh and painful is the sport of dreadful Time! Such conduct of his deserves to be condemned again and again.)

There is also another Rameni, as follows.

Rameni.

_Kripa kari guru jugat bataai, aapa khoja bhram nasaai. ||1||_
_Aapa khoja tribhivan soojhe, guru prasaad kaalasu jhujhe. ||2||_
_Shabd brahmka karo vichaara, bhav saagar tar utare paara. ||3||_
_Bahuran vikhe thagori khaai, paap punya beej nasaai. ||4||_
_Paap punya dono kar baati, janam janam jaarat he chhaati. ||5||_
_Kaisi bhaant gaaiye joga, kaise mite hariaka soga. ||6||_
_Kaho guru kaise raakhiye kaaya, ati parbal harikee maaya. ||7||_
_Kaise mite mohka fanda, kaise khijmat paave banda. ||8||_
_Paancho vairi ati bal bhanda, jine jeete sapat deep nau khanda. ||9||_
_Kaam kasaai krodh chandaala, aasha vaaran trishna kaala. ||10||_
_Lobh doomda nidra daari, mansaa chadoodi det dukh bhaari. ||11||_
_Santanki seva chit laave, patthar pooja man bhramaave. ||12||_
_Kanak kaamani kalehka bhanda, jya thaganiye sab jage danda. ||13||_
_Guru govind saar mati dini, bhali bhai jo aatam cheeni. ||14||_
_Bada bhaag so aatam jaaga, kahet kabir bhram jo bhaaga. ||15||_

Sakhi: _Re re apraadhi maanav, durlabh tera shareer, sat sukritki naavari, so kheshe daas kabir._

(1. Out of grace, the Guru showed me the technique by which I sought out and found my own self; by seeking out the self, delusion is destroyed.
2. Having sought out the self, all three worlds become clear; by the Guru's grace, one can grapple and struggle with Time.
3. Reflect upon the Word-Brahman; thereby you will cross over and land upon the far shore of the ocean of worldly existence.
4. Again, poison has deceived me repeatedly; let the very seed of sin and merit be destroyed.
5. Make both sin and merit into a single wick, and burn away the touch of birth after birth.
6. In what manner should we sing this yoga? How is the sorrow of separation from Hari to be removed?
7. Tell us, O Guru, how are we to preserve this body, for the Maya of Hari is exceedingly powerful?
8. How is the snare of delusion to be removed? How can the servant attain to Your service?
9. The five enemies are exceedingly powerful and deceitful -- they have conquered the seven islands and nine continents of the world.
10. Desire is the butcher, anger is the outcaste executioner, hope is the enemy, and craving is our own Time.
11. Greed is the tree, sleep is the harlot, and imagination is the hunting jackal whose jaws seize us from every side and give us great suffering.
12. When we think of rendering service to the saints, idol-worship throws our mind into confusion.
13. Gold and lustful woman are the very treasury of quarrel and division, by which deceitful things punish the whole world.
14. The Guru, as Govind, gave the essential wisdom, and it was well, for the soul recognized itself.
15. Great is the fortune of that soul who has awakened -- Kabir says, his delusion has fled.
Sakhi: O sinful human, this body of yours is very hard to obtain; upon the boat of true righteous action does Servant Kabir voyage.)

Servant Kabirji says that the Guru, out of grace, showed such a technique that the self, that is, the ego, was sought out and found. By seeking out the ego, the divine principle begins to become known. By the Guru's grace, one becomes able to grapple with Time. Cultivate the desire to remember God's Name, of the nature of the Word; then you will swim across to the far shore of the ocean of worldly existence. The very seed that is the bondage of sin and merit will also be destroyed. If you make both sin and merit into a single wick and burn it, you will burn away the attachments accumulated birth after birth. O Lord! O Guru! How should we render devotion to You, so that our sorrow and suffering at separation from God may be removed? O Guruji, how should we preserve our body, for the Maya of God is exceedingly powerful? How should the snare of delusion be removed, and how can the devotee render service and devotion to You? The distinction of the five kinds of enemy senses is exceedingly powerful, having conquered the ocean-girt earth of seven islands and nine continents. Desire is the butcher, and anger is the outcaste executioner; hope is the enemy, and craving is our own Death. Greed is a tree, and sleep is a harlot; and imagination, like a hunting jackal that seizes us with its jaws from every side, gives us great suffering. When we think of rendering service to saints, the worship of stone images throws our mind into confusion. Gold and a woman of desire are the very storehouse of quarrelsome division -- such deceitful things inflict their punishment upon the whole world. But the Guru, who is like Govind Himself, gave us mysterious wisdom, and thereby brought a beneficial awakening into our innermost soul. Thus, by our good fortune, our innermost soul awakened, and thereby the delusions of a devotee like Kabir were removed.

Ah! O sinful human being, this boat that is your body is exceedingly difficult to obtain; therefore, engage now in devotion, like the devotee Kabir, by means of the boat of true righteous action.

_Mahanta punyapunyena, kriteyam kaayanaustvaya, paaram duhkhodadhergatum, tara yaavanna bhidyate._ (By performing great and mighty merits, the soul has purchased this boat that is the body. O soul, cross over while this boat has not yet broken apart!)

The founding of the earth, and how Namdevji observed the Ekadashi vow -- that vow was instituted by Kripanath.

Thus the Lord gave Kailash to Rudra, gave the Brahma-abode (Brahmasadan) to Brahma, and gave the Indrasana (throne of Indra) to the gods. Then Ekadashi said, "Maharaj, I have performed a mighty feat of valor; on account of it, an intense and terrible hunger has come upon me all the more, and my body is greatly assailed by sleep and thirst." Then Vasudev said: "You shall dwell in Indra's realm; in the mortal world you shall receive great honor in My Name. On your day, in all three worlds, whoever gives up hunger, thirst, and sleep shall thereby become satisfied through you." Such a boon he gave her. He further told her, "Whoever observes your vow on your day shall attain to your own state." Having received this boon, she came into Indra's assembly. The account now tells how, having brought her into Indra's assembly, she was then brought down into the mortal world.

A certain king Rukmangad had a son Dharmangad, who was king of the city of Chandanavati; his kingdom was said to be one of great virtue and righteousness. In his city, a potter and his potter-wife once quarreled. On the tenth day they quarreled and lay down to sleep on the ground; on the Ekadashi day they both remained hungry. Because of this, Ekadashi became satisfied, and all the gods came and began raining down flowers upon that potter and his wife. Rukmangad came to learn of this matter; so he went to heaven and brought Ekadashi down into the mortal world, and greatly increased her glory. As long as the king held his own kingdom, he had this vow observed, with due rules, by all his subjects. Then the king, taking all the people of his city with him, traveled by the aerial path to have the darshan of the cave of Mahendrachal, and upon returning, settled a city together with all of them; the name of that city was Rukmangadpuri.

That dharma was set going by Rukmangad in the Satyug. In the Satyug, Rukmangad, having made all his subjects observe the Ekadashi vow, granted refuge to all of them in the city named Rukmangad. In the Tretayug it was set going by King Ambarish. In the Dwaparyug it was set going by King Chandrahas. In the Kaliyug, dharma remains untainted; all people observe this vow. There, that is, in the time of this Kaliyug, Namdevji, for the good of all, kept up a dispute in the form of one Guru's Name regarding Vishnu-bhakti. It was declared that whatever state Rukmangad attained, all people would likewise attain that same state through this vow. In this way, by spreading the vow, he began to increase the glory of devotion to Ekadashi; and for this reason Kripanath came to have Ekadashi established at Namdevji's temple. It was Shri Krishna Himself who came -- this is the account of Namdevji's testimony.

Chaupai.

_Namdev gyaaras upavaasi rahate, kashta dina do bhaari sahate. ||1||_
_Tab hari kiya braahmanka bhekha, maage anna na kare santokha. ||2||_

(1. Namdev used to remain fasting on the Ekadashi day, enduring great hardship for two days.
2. Then Hari took on the disguise of a Brahmin, and began to beg for food, refusing to be satisfied.)

_Kahat namdev dosh na deeje, doodh dahi bhaave so leeje. ||3||_
_Gyaaraske din anna na deu, aur na deu aap na leu. ||4||_
_Par upgaar na deu bataai, lage paap na hoi bhalaai. ||5||_
_Braahman bole sun re chheempa, me phir aaya jambudveepa. ||6||_
_Te mosu khechari chalaai, kahe bhookh mue kaun gat paau. ||7||_
_Naamo kahai gyaaras kyon naakhi, rukmaangadki sun le saakhi. ||8||_
_Jine tan man gyaarasi dradhaai, satal poori vaikuntha jaai. ||9||_
_Aur bhagatika maram na jaanu, ambareesh se kate aanu. ||10||_
_Braahman bole sun re bhota, saacha sabad maan le mora. ||11||_
_Jab lag girde ram nahi aape, tab lag dharam anek dradhaave. ||12||_
_Jab lag ravi nahi kare prakaasha, tab lag shashiyar kare ujaasha. ||13||_
_Teliike dhar maahishi hoi, kheer telasu jeeme soi. ||14||_
_Ekadina bhayo ghritako bheta, paaya swaad tel tab meeta. ||15||_
_Aise sab ulta vahevaara, hari vina kaun itaare paara. ||16||_
_Kahat namdev vaad na keeje, anna nahi deu doodh dahi bhaave so leeje. ||17||_
_Maskara marya parya dwij dwaara, nagar maahe paryo haahaakaara. ||18||_
_Lok kahai moodiya apraadhi, braahman maari bhagati kaun saadhi. ||19||_
_Bharmi bhagat sabe uthi bhaaga, e apraadh bado tohe laaga. ||20||_
_Aisi vaat nahi bhaave hamku, aisa harijan kare nahi kabahu. ||21||_
_Tera mukh koi dekhe paapi, aisi baat rahai kyon dhaapi. ||22||_

Sakhi: _Aap bhalaa to jag bhalaa, nahitar bhalaa na koy, ke jiv jaane aapno, ke jaake viti hoy. ||Vishraam||1||_

_Kahat namdev hamgi marhu, braahman sahit agan me jalhu._
_Tab namdev harisu moh lagaaya, dekhan log nagarka aaya. ||1||_
_Chauvaa chandan bohot mangaaya, braahmanku snaan karaaya._
_Maala chhaapa tilak banaaya, odhanku pattkul mangaaya. ||2||_
_Pitaa kahai ab kaahaa keejai, naamaa bin kaho kaise jeeje._
_Vaare pitaa kahai sun pootaa, aisi bhagati kaaheku karataa. ||3||_

(3. Namdev says: do not blame me; take milk and curd, whatever you like.
4. On the Ekadashi day I will not give grain; nor will I give it to anyone else, nor take it myself.
5. Nor will I tell you to do that favor either; even if committing this fault brought no sin, still no good would come of it.
6. The Brahmin says: Listen, O chhipa (cloth-printer), I have come again from Jambudveep.
7. You have sent me flying about; tell me, dying of hunger, what state shall I attain?
8. Namo says: why do you cast aside the Ekadashi vow? Listen to the testimony of Rukmangad:
9. Whoever fixes the Ekadashi vow firmly in body and mind attains the pure city of Vaikuntha.
10. And I do not know the secret of any other devotion; I have brought this from Ambarish.
11. The Brahmin says: Listen, O simpleton, accept my true word.
12. As long as Ram does not descend from the mountain, so long will many kinds of dharma keep being affirmed.
13. As long as the sun does not shine, so long does the moon give its light.
14. In the oilman's house there was a buffalo, which used to eat kheer mixed with oil.
15. One day it got a taste of ghee; once it tasted that flavor, the taste of oil then vanished.
16. Thus all such customs are topsy-turvy; without Hari, who can carry one across to the far shore?
17. Namdev says: do not argue with me; I will not give grain, but take milk and curd, whatever you like.
18. The trickster fell dead at the Brahmin's door; a great uproar arose in the town.
19. People say: you shaven-headed sinner! By killing a Brahmin, what devotion have you accomplished?
20. All the deluded devotees rose up and fled: this is a very grave sin that has befallen you.
21. Such a thing does not please us at all; a true devotee of Hari would never do such a thing.
22. Who would even look at your face, you sinner? How can such a matter remain hidden?
Sakhi: If you yourself are good, then the world is good to you; otherwise nothing is good. Who knows their own true self? Or upon whom does calamity fall? Pause. 1.

Namdev says: let me die; together with the Brahmin, let me burn in fire. Then Namdev fixed his devotion upon Hari; the people of the town came to watch. 1. They summoned much saffron and sandal-paste, and gave the Brahmin's body a bath; they made a garland, the sect-mark, and the tilak, and sent for a silken cloth to cover him. 2. His father says: "What is to be done now? Without Nama, tell me, how are we to live?" His father says: "Listen, my son, why do you perform such devotion?" 3.)
